focus: Which board qualities does sk-create-figjam decide today, and for each one, does generate_diagram own it, can the Mermaid model steer it, or does a use_figma extension add it afterwards?
answeredQuestions: Which board qualities does sk-create-figjam decide today, and for each one, does generate_diagram own it, can the Mermaid model steer it, or does a use_figma extension add it afterwards?

label: The packet already separates three owners explicitly - the model, generate_diagram's layout, and the additive use_figma extension - and states that a bad layout is fixed by reshaping the model, never by dragging. That ownership model is a strength to preserve, and every later improvement must land inside one of those three layers.

Layout direction is the only geometric lever the Mermaid model owns: user flow runs TD or LR on ELK, process runs TD or LR with one direction per file, architecture is LR only through a separate grid layout that mis-draws when its rules break, state runs LR or TB, and gantt's axis unit is picked by the generator.

Spacing has no rule in the model layer; every measurement in the packet is an extension clearance (40px sticky clearance, 32px section padding, 64px title clearance, 250px legend gutter, 24px tint expansion). Node-to-node, rank-to-rank and edge clearance are unowned, which is exactly the quality a reader calls cramped or airy.

Titles exist only as an optional gated extension recipe, while the generator's own name field is never defined as rendering on the board, so a reader arriving without an extension gets no title and a multi-diagram board gets no headings.

Grouping is type-gated rather than designed: sections are barred from holding generated nodes, so grouping survives only as architecture lanes, 2-6 process lanes or gantt sections, and a user flow is forbidden any subgraph. FigJam's own section, the grouping affordance a reader recognises instantly, is usable only for legend stickies.

Density is a node count only - 9 nodes and one accent for a user flow, 9 nodes and 12 connectors in general, 12 gantt tasks with 5 parallel bars per section - so a diagram can pass its budget and still be unreadable because nothing measures content against area, connector ratio, longest path or crossings.

A multi-diagram board has no composition rule: later diagrams reuse the fileKey and the tag is keyed by diagram name for rollback, but nothing sets the gap between diagrams, a shared heading band, a numbered reading order or which diagram a reader meets first.

Colour roles are deliberate and well recorded, but architecture takes no colour from the model and sequence, state and ER lose Mermaid styling entirely, so four of seven types are effectively colourless and the style guide's honest list of what did not translate leaves no replacement rule for the hierarchy work those tokens used to do.

Text size is explicitly not steerable - the generator sets FigJam's font and the tool cannot change it afterwards - so the only typographic levers are the 40-character one-line label cap, shape count, accent and label length, and both a board title and a node label render at the same size.

Read-back verifies existence, connector endpoints, end caps and label text and explicitly refuses to read direction from position, which leaves reading order, adjacency and spacing unverified: a board whose nodes landed in an order no reader would follow still passes read-back.

The board quality scorecard scores seven dimensions out of 14, but Layout is a crossing counter and Clarity is three reader questions, so no dimension is specifically about whitespace, grouping, sectioning, title presence, edge-label placement or whether the board has a beginning, and a board can pass at 12 of 14 while reading poorly.

The packet is already strong where comparable skills are weak: it refuses to invent content, caps a decision at three labelled exits, sets detail level and audience before modelling, never restyles a generated node, and records measured departures with the ratios behind each refusal. None of the ranked changes should touch these.

direction: Recover the 4px grid and node-size tokens from sk-design-diagram as FigJam rules
reason: The grid governs a renderer this packet does not own; style-guide.md records the omission deliberately, so re-adding the token would create a rule nothing can enforce. Replace its hierarchy role instead.

direction: Re-propose 'the generator owns layout, never move a generated node'
reason: Already the packet's strongest guardrail and already part of the implemented 017 change set; recorded as a strength rather than a gap.
